source: Natural Earth master (data frozen June 2022, v5.2.0-pre): ne_10m/110m_admin_0_countries, ne_50m_admin_0_breakaway_disputed_areas, POV variants. Method: point-in-polygon of representative cities. Raw data: data/ne_consistency_matrix.json in the research repo.

absorbed_clean.label: Absorbed into occupier — no dispute marker
absorbed_clean.description: Territory merged into the occupying state's polygon; that polygon is typed a clean "Sovereign country".

absorbed_marked.label: Absorbed into occupier — dispute marker on polygon
absorbed_marked.description: Territory inside the occupier's polygon, but the polygon itself carries TYPE="Disputed".

kept_dejure.label: Kept with de jure state despite de facto loss
kept_dejure.description: De facto control lost, but NE keeps the territory in the de jure state's polygon.

own_unit.label: Own separate unit
own_unit.description: NE carves the territory out as its own admin-0 entity — occupier's polygon unchanged.

split_defacto.label: Split along de facto lines
split_defacto.description: Divided between controlling states along lines of control.

rows.rule_followed: Yes — the only Russia-linked territory where it is
rows.note: The only 21st-century annexation of a UN member's territory absorbed into the annexing state's polygon. NE's own USA-POV and UKR-POV variant files put Crimea in Ukraine; the ISO-POV leaves it unassigned. Only the default — the file every downstream library ships — awards it to Russia.

rows.de_facto: DNR/Russia since 2014 — same year as Crimea
rows.note: Disputed-layer entry: "Self admin.; Claimed by Ukraine", SOVEREIGNT=Ukraine. Same war, same aggressor, same year as Crimea — opposite treatment.

rows.de_facto: LNR/Russia since 2014 — same year as Crimea
Russia (Feb–May 2022, before NE's June 2022 data freeze)
rows.note: Under full Russian control when NE last touched its data — polygons unchanged. Under NE's revealed rule (sovereignty flips on formal annexation), the Sept 2022 "annexations" would flip these to Russia in any future NE update.
14 years of de facto separation at data freeze — never reassigned.
30 years of de facto separation at data freeze — never reassigned.
Fully Azerbaijani since the Sept 2023 offensive; Artsakh dissolved 1 Jan 2024. NE's assignment now matches reality — but it predates those events, so when authored it contradicted the de facto rule.

rows.rule_followed: Partially — de facto recognized without rewarding Turkey
rows.note: The exact precedent for Crimea: armed invasion → separate unit, occupier's polygon unchanged. NE chose not to apply it.

rows.rule_followed: Partially — own unit with dispute marker

rows.ne_assignment: Israel — but Israel's entire polygon is TYPE="Disputed"
rows.rule_followed: Yes — with a country-level dispute marker
rows.note: Closest parallel to Crimea (unrecognized annexation). Difference: Israel's polygon is typed Disputed; Russia's is a clean Sovereign country.
Post-WWII case; disputed-layer entry exists ("Claimed by Japan").

rows.ne_assignment: Split: Moroccan zone → Morocco; SADR zone → own unit, TYPE=Indeterminate
Split along lines of control; extensive disputed-layer coverage

rows.rule_followed: Mixed — separate ADMIN unit, occupier sovereignty

headline: Of the 8 Russia-linked occupied territories in Natural Earth's data, the "de facto control" rule is applied to exactly one — the only one whose reassignment benefits Russia's sovereignty claim: Crimea.
